children: Chicago soybean futures extended losses to a second session on Tuesday, weighed by the approaching completion of harvests.
Wheat futures inched higher amid slower-than-average winter wheat planting, while corn rose for a third session.
The most-traded soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT)
was down 0.12% at $12.27-1/2 a bushel at 0200 GMT. CBOT wheat
added 0.21% at $5.88-1/4 a bushel and CBOT corn corn
The US soybean harvest was 96% complete as of Sunday, a point ahead of average, while corn harvesting was slower than average at 88% done, the US Department of Agriculture said on Monday

The US soybean crush in October jumped to the largest for any month on record as an accelerating soy harvest replenished crushing supplies, while soyoil stocks rebounded after hitting lowest in nearly 12 years a month earlier, NOPA data showed

Winter wheat planting for the crop to be harvested in 2027 is nearly finished at 92% complete as of Sunday, up from 89% a week earlier but behind the five-year average of 94% done. Analysts, on average, expected the USDA to report planting at 94% complete, with estimates ranging from 94% to 95%

Winter wheat crop conditions improved by more than expected to 53% good to excellent, up from 49% a week earlier and above the five-year average of 45% good to excellent. Analysts polled by Reuters, on average, expected the USDA to report that 50% of the crop was in good-to-excellent shape as of Sunday, with estimates ranging from 49% to 53%
Euronext wheat rose on Monday as euro weakness and continuing war disruption to Black Sea shipping boosted short-term export prospects in Western Europe

Asian shares followed Wall Street lower on Tuesday, weighed down by weakness in technology companies after the US stepped up efforts to curb China's access to advanced AI chips, escalating the race for technological dominance.
